logistics.eligibility: Open to organizations in the Claude Partner Network. No formal course prerequisite is stated on the public listing, so the learning path is recommended rather than required.
onvue: Supported computer with webcam, microphone and speaker, and exactly one display
At least 6 Mbps down and 2 Mbps up
No VPNs, no virtual machines, no corporate or public networks, no headphones
Check-in opens 30 minutes early: identity photos plus a 360-degree room scan
The session is recorded; you must stay alone and in view, must not read aloud, must not touch a phone or record the screen, and may not leave except for an approved break

learningPath.intro: Four courses, in this order, on the public Claude Partner Network Learning Path. All free. The path calls itself an introductory foundation and the first step toward unlocking certification. Course durations are not published, so budget by module count rather than by minutes.

courses.title: Introduction to agent skills
courses.summary: Build, configure, share, distribute and troubleshoot reusable Markdown Skills in Claude Code.
courses.why: Directly feeds Task 3.2: SKILL.md frontmatter, context: fork, allowed-tools, argument-hint, and the project-versus-user scoping decision.

courses.title: Building with the Claude API
courses.summary: The broadest single exam-aligned course. Assumes Python and basic JSON.
courses.why: Covers tool schemas and results, parallel tools, structured output, evaluation and MCP, which is most of Domains 1, 2 and 4.
modules: Accessing Claude with the API (authentication, API requests, multi-turn chat, system prompts, temperature, streaming)
Prompt evaluation (dataset generation, model-based and code-based grading)
Prompt engineering techniques (XML, examples, structured output)
Tool use with Claude (tool schemas, tool results, parallel tools, web search)
RAG and Agentic Search (chunking, embeddings, BM25, contextual retrieval)
Features of Claude (thinking, images, PDFs, citations, caching, code execution)
Model Context Protocol (clients, servers, resources, prompts)
Anthropic apps: Claude Code and computer use

courses.title: Introduction to Model Context Protocol
courses.summary: Build MCP servers and clients from scratch in Python. The three primitives: tools, resources, prompts.
courses.why: Domain 2 is 18% of the exam and turns on knowing when something is a tool versus a resource.
modules: Introduction: welcome, introducing MCP, MCP clients
Hands-on with MCP servers: project setup, defining tools, Server Inspector
Connecting with MCP clients: implementing a client, defining and accessing resources, defining prompts, prompts in the client

courses.title: Claude Code in Action
courses.summary: From short interactive tasks to long, less-supervised Claude Code workflows you can trust.
courses.why: The closest match to Domain 3 and to the long-session context management in Domain 5.

notOnPath.title: Model Context Protocol: Advanced Topics
notOnPath.note: Free follow-on. Sampling, notifications, roots, JSON message types, stdio, Streamable HTTP, HTTP state. Useful depth for Domain 2, but not on the path.

notOnPath.title: Building with the Claude Agent SDK
notOnPath.note: Not one of the four path cards, yet Domain 1 is 27% of the exam and is almost entirely Agent SDK. Fill this gap from the docs and by building.

notOnPath.title: AI Fluency
notOnPath.note: General public Academy material. Not exam-relevant.

studySequence: Complete the four path courses in order.
Read the official exam guide end to end. It is the blueprint and it names the traps.
Build one Messages API tool loop driven by stop_reason, and one MCP server plus client.
Configure a real Claude Code project: CLAUDE.md hierarchy, .claude/rules/ with globs, a skill with context: fork, hooks, permissions, one MCP server.
Close blueprint gaps from the docs and cookbook, domain by domain.
Finish with timed scenario practice and an error log categorized by domain.

tensions.intro: Four architectural tensions worth holding in mind. Scenario items are usually asking you to resolve one of them.

items.b: An Agent SDK loop handles unknown steps. A fixed workflow is cheaper, more testable and more predictable. Reach for the loop only when the path genuinely varies.
A very large window does not remove the need for retrieval, trimming, compaction or attention to position. Bigger is not the fix for attention dilution.
Structured output guarantees parseability, never factual accuracy or policy compliance. Syntax errors go away; wrong values do not.
Hooks and prerequisite gates guarantee. Prompts and few-shot examples persuade. Financial and compliance requirements need the first kind.

distractorPatterns: Using an autonomous agent for a deterministic transform.
Adding infrastructure (a classifier, a routing layer, an ML model) where a text or configuration change fixes the root cause.
Prompt-based fixes where a deterministic guarantee is required.
Fixing a downstream component that was working correctly within its assignment.
A bigger model or a bigger context window for an attention or decomposition problem.
Invented features that do not exist, such as CLAUDE_HEADLESS, --batch, or .claude/config.json.
Shifting the burden onto humans instead of fixing the system.
Self-reported confidence or sentiment used as a proxy for complexity.
communityCaveats: Third-party practice banks are diagnostic material, not exam truth. One widely linked guide still quotes a stale $99 fee against the live $125.
Claims of exact overlap with live questions are red flags and violate the NDA you accept before the exam begins.
The public listing does not state multiple-choice versus multiple-response ratios. The official guide does say each item states how many responses to select.
Course durations are not published anywhere public. Ignore any source that quotes them.
